parts.note: the prefix re- means again, as in redo
to match is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Someone agrees once more to play a second fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A second contest between the same opponents is a return game, the replay that settles who is better.

parts.note: read as rear plus -ed, the word suggests having been given a back end, while the real sense is brought up, raised or rose up on hind legs

explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic reading takes backed as given a rear; the plain sense is raised, as children or as a horse rising on its hind legs.

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
ST, short for street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: A description of two paths that are both lowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two ways' supplies both pieces: MODE (a manner) and ST (street, a road).
explanation.definitionFit: Humble and unassuming people are self-effacing, a near synonym.

clue.text: It has it ups and downs on the way to the sea

definitions.text: It has it ups and downs on the way to the sea

parts.words: It has it ups and downs on the way to the sea
parts.note: a stream flowing seaward whose water level rises and falls twice a day with the tides, rather than a bumpy road

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hilly journey; the ups and downs are tides. 'It ups' is the clue as held, presumably meant as 'its ups'.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercourse near its estuary rises and falls with the tide as it flows to the coast.

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A colouring agent produced naturally by a lichen.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish plant extract used to colour hair and skin is a dye.

clue.text: Eager to have a drink with this

definitions.text: to have a drink with this
definitions.meaning: split as a thirst, the thing that makes you want to drink

explanation.definitionFit: Being athirst is being keen for something, and a thirst is what makes one reach for a glass.

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters of radon fly into a new order
unstable letters do not hold their arrangement, so made is rearranged

explanation.surface: A radioactive gas blowing up has made a group of stars unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams side by side: 'exploding' turns RADON into ANDRO and 'unstable' turns MADE into MEDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation named after the chained princess of Greek myth is a group of stars.

clue.text: Second student leaving city has a dance

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so one letter is removed from the city

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England
L, the learner-driver plate, stands for student

explanation.surface: A student moves away from a city and takes up a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: HULL is a port city in northern England. 'Second' tells you it is the second of its two Ls that goes; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian swaying dance is the well-known example.

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties

indicators.note: putting the word into into another order rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A staff roster is reorganised into a different sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn or revolution is a rotation, as in a wheel's spin.

parts.note: not a fixed-price menu but food eaten in front of the television set

explanation.definitionFit: A prepared tray of food heated and eaten while watching television is a meal tied to the set.

parts.note: an aide is an assistant or auxiliary

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word delivery

explanation.surface: A hospital helper assisted at their first birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Aided is a synonym for assisted.

clue.text: Saw endlessly dull article inside had little rounded lumps

indicators.note: inside puts the trimmed word and the article within the synonym for saw

parts.note: to see something is to note it, so saw is noted

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the word dull

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A carpenter's saw, endlessly blunt, produced knobbly lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from dull; 'inside' then sets that and the article within the synonym for saw. 'Saw' looks like the tool, but it is the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodules are small rounded swellings, so something covered with them is lumpy.

indicators.note: the country's name comes out of the letters of salad-lover, made from them by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone who loves salad comes from a certain nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' signals that the country's letters are made from salad-lover rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American republic is a nation.

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a stunt is a daring or risky act

explanation.surface: Amazing spectators with an endless daredevil performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' drops the final T of STUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to stagger or daze them with surprise.

parts.note: reads like calling off a wedding, but means ending a telephone connection or unplugging something engaged

explanation.definitionFit: To sever a link, as cutting a call or unplugging a device, is to break a connection.

clue.text: It's the last you'll see of the serial

definitions.text: It's the last you'll see of the serial

parts.words: It's the last you'll see of the serial
parts.note: the closing instalment of a television drama series, after which no more is shown

explanation.definitionFit: The concluding instalment of a series ends it, so nothing further of the serial appears.

clue.text: A very heavy fall of snow

definitions.text: A very heavy fall of snow

parts.words: A very heavy fall of snow
parts.note: not a blizzard but a mass of snow sliding down a mountainside

explanation.definitionFit: A snowslide is a huge mass of snow crashing down a slope, a heavy fall in the other sense.

clue.text: Patriot said drink must go first

indicators.note: said means the drink is spoken, and only its sound is kept

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink
taken as written
first is written 1st, and the figure 1 reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: A nationalist insists the gin must be poured before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes GIN sound like JIN; 'first' as 1ST gives IST, the 1 read as an I. 'must' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jingoist is an aggressive, flag-waving nationalist, a patriot taken to excess.

clue.text: Most inclined to be going up perhaps

definitions.meaning: describing the climb that is hardest, the sharpest ascent

explanation.definitionFit: The sharpest slope is the most tilted, and the hardest climb on a hill is up its sharpest face.

definitions.meaning: literally sitting in the pans of a weighing device

explanation.definitionFit: An undecided outcome hangs uncertain, and a balance is a weighing device.

indicators.note: about means going around, so the phrase for employed surrounds the numeral

parts.note: to set on workers is to take them on, employ them
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A church worker was hired at around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts X inside SET ON, after SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton looks after a church building and graveyard, a church officer.

indicators.note: letters spread out and reassembled are rearranged

explanation.surface: Faced with a bigger buffet, someone eats nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food entirely is to starve.

definitions.meaning: a part-song for several unaccompanied voices

explanation.definitionFit: A glee is a short part-song for voices, and glee is also joy, here malicious joy at others' troubles.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for one temperature scale, as in 98.6 F

explanation.definitionFit: The temperature scale on which water freezes at 32 degrees is abbreviated F.

clue.text: Not a subject needed at school

definitions.meaning: a monarch, who rules subjects rather than being one
a straight-edged measuring stick in a pupil's pencil case

explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign governs subjects, and a measuring rule is standard school equipment.

indicators.note: turned means the word for stake is read backwards

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A gambler's wager is overturned on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the volcanic mountain in Sicily.

clue.text: These things cannot be told apart

definitions.text: These things cannot be told apart

parts.words: These things cannot be told apart
parts.note: describes items or twins so alike that no one can distinguish them

explanation.definitionFit: Exactly alike objects are indistinguishable, so no one can tell which is which.

indicators.note: produced means the letters of a tree are worked into something new

explanation.surface: An orchard tree yields an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges A TREE. An eater is an apple grown for eating raw rather than cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert fruit for eating raw rather than cooking is called an eater.

clue.text: Measure the strength of a solution — or the speed of a small bird?

definitions.text: Measure the strength of a solution

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A chemistry task, or a question about how fast a tiny bird flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the speed of a small bird' puts speed first, but the possessive 'of' means the bird's speed, so the bird comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, titration finds a dissolved substance's concentration by adding a reagent.

definitions.meaning: the attendants following an important person
those who follow behind, the followers of a dignitary

explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary's entourage, the people who follow behind, is a train.
